column1: # edge-containers-1.tsv — container IDENTITY edge cases: eq vs deq over
# compounds, and the per-call literal-identity family (miscompile-A
# mechanism, design/legacy/MISCOMPILE-HUNT-FINDINGS.0.ignore §A).
# `eq` on non-scalars is CONTAINER IDENTITY (eng/go/compare.go
# ExactEqual → sameContainer): a MapPayload identifies by its
# *OrderedMap pointer, a ListPayload by its backing element array, a
# flex node by its store pointer, a class/record instance by its
# Fields map (flatInstanceParts). `deq` is structural. Two literal
# twins are never eq; a dup/def alias always is. The ONE deliberate
# exception: an empty list has no backing array to alias by, so ALL
# empty plain lists are eq (sameContainer treats them as the single
# empty list). Empty MAPS do NOT unify — each {} is a fresh
# OrderedMap pointer. Empty FLEX lists do not unify either — the
# FlexListData store pointer IS the identity.
# A container literal in a fn body is constructed FRESH per call
# (per-call identity — the miscompile-A fix): two calls are deq but
# never eq. A fn body that READS an enclosing binding returns the
# SHARED container — every call is eq to the source.
# §1  literal twins are never eq — eq is identity, deq is structure

same for longer lists
two map literals are two containers

empty list vs empty map — different families

no cross-family leaf coercion
differing content is not deq
